notes: Historical inputs (2023–2025): Revenue and EBIT use TE Connectivity’s consolidated statement of operations (net sales and operating income). ([te.com](https://www.te.com/content/dam/te-com/documents/about-te/our-company/global/annual-report/te-connectivity-annual-report-2025.pdf))

Historical D&A and capex: Depreciation & amortization taken from consolidated cash flow adjustments; capex taken as absolute capital expenditures from the FY2025 annual report disclosures. ([te.com](https://www.te.com/content/dam/te-com/documents/about-te/our-company/global/annual-report/te-connectivity-annual-report-2025.pdf))

Working capital (NWC) construction: NWC is computed as (Accounts receivable + Inventories + Prepaid & other current assets) − (Accounts payable + Accrued & other current liabilities), excluding cash and excluding short-term debt from current liabilities. FY23–FY25 computed from year-end balance sheet line items. ([te.com](https://www.te.com/content/dam/te-com/documents/about-te/our-company/global/annual-report/te-connectivity-annual-report-2025.pdf))

Tax rate: TE’s GAAP effective tax rate is highly non-linear (including valuation allowance impacts); base-case uses a normalized tax_rate=0.22. ([te.com](https://www.te.com/content/dam/te-com/documents/about-te/our-company/global/annual-report/te-connectivity-annual-report-2025.pdf))
WACC: base-case wacc uses a market-data-derived WACC of ~10.14% (0.1014) as a starting point, then bull/bear adjust modestly. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/tel/statistics/))

NOL balance: nol_balance uses net operating loss (tax-effected carryforward) totals from the FY2025 note on tax loss/credit carryforwards; treated as a single aggregate NOL balance for modeling. ([te.com](https://www.te.com/content/dam/te-com/documents/about-te/our-company/global/annual-report/te-connectivity-annual-report-2025.pdf))

Investments field: investments is set to null because the prompt’s schema expects a separate value, but the filings’ cash-flow investing line items are not consistently labeled in a way that cleanly maps to a single 'investments' scalar for this DCF pipeline without additional definition (kept as null to avoid inventing mapping).
Scenario overrides: bull/bear modify only the forecast drivers and select valuation assumptions (wacc, terminal_growth, target_ebit_margin); base operating model structure otherwise remains the same.

catalysts: Sustained order strength and conversion into FY26 revenue and earnings (recent Q1 orders and guidance reinforce execution momentum). ([investors.te.com](https://investors.te.com/news-releases/press-release-details/2026/TE-Connectivity-announces-first-quarter-results-for-fiscal-year-2026/default.aspx))
Further margin expansion from operational excellence and mix shift toward higher-value connectivity/power and data-centric applications.

Potential tax/valuation allowance developments that reduce normalized cash tax drag (base-case tax rate is normalized vs volatile GAAP effective rates). ([te.com](https://www.te.com/content/dam/te-com/documents/about-te/our-company/global/annual-report/te-connectivity-annual-report-2025.pdf))
company_overview: TE Connectivity is a global industrial technology leader focused on connectivity and sensor solutions used across transportation, energy networks, data centers, and industrial automation.
The company reports results across two main operating segments (Industrial Solutions and Transportation Solutions) with exposure to secular demand themes such as AI/data and power connectivity.
TE’s strategy emphasizes innovation, operational execution, and capital allocation to support profitable growth across cyclical end markets.
current_context: FY26 Q1 ended Dec. 26, 2025: net sales of $4.7 billion (+22% YoY reported; +15% organically) with adjusted EPS of $2.72 (+33% YoY). ([investors.te.com](https://investors.te.com/news-releases/press-release-details/2026/TE-Connectivity-announces-first-quarter-results-for-fiscal-year-2026/default.aspx))

Record quarterly orders of $5.1 billion (+28% YoY; +9% sequentially) and management guidance reiterates double-digit sales/adjusted earnings growth expectations into FY26 Q2. ([investors.te.com](https://investors.te.com/news-releases/press-release-details/2026/TE-Connectivity-announces-first-quarter-results-for-fiscal-year-2026/default.aspx))

FY26 Q2 outlook: sales ~ $4.7 billion (+13% reported; +6% organic) and adjusted EPS ~ $2.65 (+20% YoY). ([investors.te.com](https://investors.te.com/news-releases/press-release-details/2026/TE-Connectivity-announces-first-quarter-results-for-fiscal-year-2026/default.aspx))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth assumes a deceleration from FY25’s rebound into a mid-single-digit long-run profile, consistent with a maturing cycle rather than a perpetual high-growth phase.

EBIT margin is modeled to expand modestly from the FY25 level toward a ~0.195 steady-state target, reflecting operational leverage seen in recent quarters. ([te.com](https://www.te.com/content/dam/te-com/documents/about-te/our-company/global/annual-report/te-connectivity-annual-report-2025.pdf))

Sustained reinvestment is represented via normalized capex intensity (~4.9%–5.2% of sales) and D&A intensity near the recent range. ([te.com](https://www.te.com/content/dam/te-com/documents/about-te/our-company/global/annual-report/te-connectivity-annual-report-2025.pdf))

Working capital intensity is kept structurally stable/slightly improving in the base case (NWC as % of sales gradually rises versus FY25 cash-efficient period), reducing valuation sensitivity to large timing swings. ([te.com](https://www.te.com/content/dam/te-com/documents/about-te/our-company/global/annual-report/te-connectivity-annual-report-2025.pdf))
key_risks: End-market downturn risk (notably automotive/industrial demand variability) causing revenue growth to undershoot base-case.
Working capital or pricing/commodity volatility creating margin and cash conversion risk versus forecast assumptions.

Tax/regulatory changes and global minimum tax implementation affecting effective cash taxes and deferred tax utilization. ([te.com](https://www.te.com/content/dam/te-com/documents/about-te/our-company/global/annual-report/te-connectivity-annual-report-2025.pdf))

valuation_summary: The DCF base case is built on observable FY23–FY25 financial history (revenue, operating income/EBIT, depreciation & amortization, capex) and conservative forward operating assumptions. ([te.com](https://www.te.com/content/dam/te-com/documents/about-te/our-company/global/annual-report/te-connectivity-annual-report-2025.pdf))

Comparable multiples are included as directional context using peer EV/EBITDA, EV/Sales, and forward P/E (treated here as NTM proxies based on source conventions). ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/aph/statistics/))
Terminal value uses Gordon growth with a moderate long-run growth rate (economically consistent for a mature industrial connectivity/electronics franchise).
